s1.syndrome_frame: Acute decompensated heart failure with arrhythmia
salient_findings: New York Heart Association functional class IV symptoms
key_facts: Patient has a history of ischemic cardiomyopathy
Ejection fraction is 10%
Patient has a single-chamber primary prevention implantable cardioverter-defibrillator
Patient was previously on amiodarone treatment
Heart rate is 106 beats/min
Blood pressure is 96/58 mm Hg
N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide is markedly elevated
Creatinine levels are elevated
ECG shows a wide QRS rhythm with atypical left bundle-branch block morphology
Electrophysiology study confirmed dual tachycardia

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute decompensated heart failure with arrhythmia
salient_findings: New York Heart Association functional class IV symptoms
key_facts: Patient has a history of ischemic cardiomyopathy
Ejection fraction is 10%
Patient has a single-chamber primary prevention implantable cardioverter-defibrillator
Patient was previously on amiodarone treatment
Heart rate is 106 beats/min
Blood pressure is 96/58 mm Hg
N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide is markedly elevated
Creatinine levels are elevated
ECG shows a wide QRS rhythm with atypical left bundle-branch block morphology
Electrophysiology study confirmed dual tachycardia

differentials: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
Plakoglobin mutation-related arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
per_call: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
Plakoglobin mutation-related arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy

shortlist.label: Tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of ischemic cardiomyopathy, low ejection fraction, and is experiencing tachycardia

shortlist.label: Ischemic cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of ischemic cardiomyopathy and low ejection fraction

shortlist.label: Dilated cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a low ejection fraction and signs of volume overload

shortlist.label: Ventricular tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Electrophysiology study confirmed dual tachycardia and patient has a wide QRS rhythm

shortlist.label: Cardiac tamponade
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has elevated jugular venous pressure and signs of substantial volume overload

raw.rationale: The patient's worsening symptoms, decreased ejection fraction, and markedly elevated N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide, combined with the ECG findings of a wide QRS rhythm and the electrophysiology study confirming dual tachycardia, suggest that the patient's cardiomyopathy is being exacerbated by the tachycardia.

rejected.label: Ischemic cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of ischemic cardiomyopathy, the current presentation suggests an acute exacerbation due to tachycardia rather than a pure ischemic cause.

rejected.label: Dilated cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The patient's ejection fraction and symptoms are consistent with a cardiomyopathy, but the specific diagnosis of dilated cardiomyopathy is not as directly supported by the tachycardia and electrophysiology findings as tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy.

rejected.label: Ventricular tachycardia
rejected.why: Ventricular tachycardia is a possible cause of the patient's symptoms, but it does not fully explain the decreased ejection fraction and other signs of cardiomyopathy.

rejected.label: Cardiac tamponade
rejected.why: There is no mention of specific findings suggestive of cardiac tamponade, such as a pericardial effusion on imaging or pulsus paradoxus, making this diagnosis less likely.
